entries.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
entries.snippet: Ukraine's leader had said the deal with Russia to release diesel into the US would help Moscow fund the war.

entries.title: Pope Leo to have surgery after lump found on lung
entries.snippet: The 71-year-old pontiff said the nodule was identified "at a very early stage".

entries.title: Homes and bridges swept away as fresh floods hit Nepal
entries.snippet: Nepal is still trying to recover from catastrophic floods that hit less than two months ago, leaving thousands dead and missing.

entries.title: Delhi sees more protests as freed 'cockroach' group's leaders vow to fight on
entries.snippet: Hundreds of people who came out on the streets despite the police's restrictions were detained on Sunday.

entries.title: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
entries.snippet: The White House had blocked access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, leading them to restrict pool coverage.

entries.title: Children among 109 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
entries.snippet: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 350 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.

entries.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
entries.snippet: The team en route to the suspected crash site aim finally to solve the mystery of her 1937 disappearance.

entries.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
entries.snippet: Pike's lawyers say she is "grateful" to the medical team who cared for her after she survived two lethal injections last month.

entries.title: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people
entries.snippet: Volodymyr Zelensky says the attack, which left children dead, was Russia expressing its "thanks" for a US diesel deal.

entries.title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
entries.snippet: Former students launched their own investigation, spending years collecting evidence and testimonies from others who say they were abused by the headteacher.

entries.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
entries.snippet: Polish police had already deployed to schools after a female caretaker was killed and several others injured in two earlier attacks in two days.

entries.title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
entries.snippet: Navi Pillay says the Trump administrations' sweeping penalties on the international tribunal were "unheard of".

entries.title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case
entries.snippet: Philadelphia police said the tip was "flagged as spam", but criticised the tech company for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach.

entries.title: Drone strike by Sudan paramilitary kills 41 near Ethiopian border, rights group says
entries.snippet: Eight children are said to be among those killed by the strike, which hit a gathering of displaced people.

entries.title: US country music star Ella Langley cancels show due to 'security threat'
entries.snippet: Police say they checked the concert venue in Tulsa, Oklahoma but "could not find any threat".

entries.title: Flydubai attacker began a 'drift towards extremism and terrorism' in Australia, UAE says
entries.snippet: The United Arab Emirates' attorney-general also alleges the co-pilot was trying to crash the plane into Tel Aviv's airport.

entries.title: Three men found guilty of murdering Australian brothers and US friend in Mexico
entries.snippet: Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend Carter Rhoad were on a surf trip when they were killed in an apparent botched robbery.

entries.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he would not watch it
entries.snippet: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

entries.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
entries.snippet: The left-wing candidate won a narrow victory in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, exit polls show.

entries.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
entries.snippet: Often dubbed "Russia's Google", the tech firm admits customers may experience disruption to digital services due to the attacks.

entries.title: Hurricane Simon nears Mexico with 155 mph winds and flooding fears
entries.snippet: The eye of Hurricane Simon was just off the Pacific coast of Mexico early Sunday and was expected to move inland later in the day as an extremely powerful storm.

entries.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
entries.snippet: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.

entries.title: A heroic, 7-day bike ride made this teen a global star. Where is she now?
entries.snippet: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

entries.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
entries.snippet: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.

entries.title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
entries.snippet: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.

entries.title: In one of the country's most competitive districts, a Democrat tries to keep her seat
entries.snippet: In a highly competitive Washington congressional race, the incumbent Democrat has angered part of her party base and the Trump-backed Republican challenger faces backlash against the party in power.

entries.title: It's taking longer to find a new job after losing one
entries.snippet: People who lose their jobs in this economy are taking longer to find new work. Nearly four in ten people exhaust their unemployment benefits before they land a new job.

entries.title: Attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and wounded over 300 more, Saudi authorities say
entries.snippet: Saudi authorities say the latest attack on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, has killed 12 people and injured over 300. Their statement says the dead on Saturday included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an E

entries.title: Christa Pike discharged from the hospital and back in prison
entries.snippet: Pike's attorneys say she is grateful for the care of first responders and her medical team.

entries.title: Bayeux Tapestry's London tour spurs enthusiasts to Battle of Hastings reenactment
entries.snippet: A reenactment of the Battle of Hastings, which took place almost a millennium ago, is drawing crowds of enthusiasts in the UK.

entries.title: What to expect as Hurricane Isaias bears down on the Gulf Coast as a major storm
entries.snippet: Hurricane Isaias has strengthened into a Category 3 hurricane as it heads toward the Gulf Coast. Residents are rushing to prepare for the storm, which is packing winds up to 120 mph and is expected to make landfall Friday night. Amna Nawaz speaks with Michael Brennan, director of

entries.title: ICE shooting of man in New York with child in his car sparks outrage
entries.snippet: An investigation is underway after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot a man in New York City Thursday. Federal authorities say 28-year-old Oscar Belgal attempted to ram officers with his vehicle when they tried to detain him. ICE agents then fired at his car, wh

entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, Trump says he struck a deal with Russia for millions of tons of diesel in a bid to lower U.S. energy prices, Katie Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary, the Pentagon's plans to livestream an execution has drawn strong reac

entries.title: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize after long career of investigating war crimes
entries.snippet: International human rights lawyer Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The Nobel Committee said it chose her as "institutions of international law are under political attack." Hours later, the Trump administration sanctioned the International Criminal Court, where Pil

entries.title: How local officials are testing voting machines to ensure election integrity
entries.snippet: Midterm election season culminates on one important Election Day, but voting is already underway in many states. For the local officials who run elections, the work started even earlier. Liz Landers reports on how they prepare for voting and why they say voters should trust the p

entries.title: 'It was a definite quid pro quo.' GOP donor who accused Guilfoyle of corruption speaks out
entries.snippet: A Republican donor is accusing U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle of asking for $100,000 in exchange for access to top Trump administration officials. Amna Nawaz speaks with Eric Deters, a former Kentucky congressional candidate, about the requests for payment and the a

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on the fight for Senate control in battleground states
entries.snippet: Candidates for U.S. Senate in three battleground states faced off in fiery debates Thursday night that frequently veered into personal attacks. David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the battle for c

entries.title: Ke Huy Quan reflects on his family's escape from post-war Vietnam on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: Actor Ke Huy Quan went from arriving in America as a refugee to starring in Indiana Jones and The Goonies. Decades later, he made an Oscar-winning comeback. In the latest episode of our PBS News podcast "Settle In," Amna Nawaz spoke with him about his debut memoir "Never Say Die,

entries.title: Trump strikes deal with Putin for Russian diesel in sharp reversal of U.S. policy ahead of midterms
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

entries.title: Legal path seems narrow to challenge livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution, experts say
entries.snippet: Broadcasting the event worldwide isn't mentioned in the Army rules governing how rare military executions are carried out. But that doesn't mean there is a viable legal path to oppose it by anyone besides Nidal Malik Hasan.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Graham set to debate Senate challengers Andrews, Whitener in South Carolina
entries.snippet: South Carolina Republican Sen. Darline Graham will face off in a debate Sunday against Democratic challenger Dr. Annie Andrews and Libertarian candidate Kasie Whitener.

entries.title: WATCH: Vance says he's 'not going to be watching' livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
entries.snippet: Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on Friday whether the Pentagon will livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan in December but told reporters that if it is livestreamed, "I'm not going to be watching it."

entries.title: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
entries.snippet: The inquiry will include a hearing at the White House Nov. 5, President Donald Trump said in a written memo, that Cook "shall" attend to answer questions from the committee.

entries.title: As Blanche hits the campaign trail, new DOJ memo relaxes rules around political conduct for Senate-approved appointees
entries.snippet: The Department of Justice is making it easier for Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Senate-confirmed DOJ appointees to participate in political activities, according to a new internal memo obtained by PBS News.

entries.title: Time for term limits? Dems in majority could have familiar faces in key roles
entries.snippet: Democrats hope to bring a new agenda to the House next year if they take the majority, but they will most likely do so with many of the same faces that have steered their party's legislative work for a decade or more.

entries.title: Trump wants Talarico and Paxton to debate. Talarico couldn't be happier
entries.snippet: When Democratic nominee James Talarico stopped holding campaign events in the Texas Senate race, his Republican opponent Ken Paxton saw an opening to pounce.

entries.title: The midterms stakes are high for these 2028 presidential prospects
entries.snippet: As most of the political world focuses on next month's midterm elections, the shadow primary for the 2028 presidential contest is quietly playing out in public view.

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: Trump rallies with New York's GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman
entries.snippet: At a political moment where Republicans are hoping to capture centrists wary of an ascendent progressive left, Blakeman has instead embraced the president and his aggressive conservative tactics.

entries.title: Trump's memorial arch faces a new lawsuit from Arlington County, Virginia
entries.snippet: The Arlington County Board in Virginia filed a lawsuit Thursday opposing the construction of the Triumphal Arch, becoming the first governmental body to take legal action against President Donald Trump's planned monument.

entries.title: The plague never went away. Cases are reported in parts of Africa and the U.S. nearly every year
entries.snippet: The plague, the rare bacterial infection infamously known for killing tens of millions in 14th-century Europe, never went away. It is now easily treated with antibiotics.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: A migrant boat sank off the coast of Djibouti with the UN reporting over 200 people dead or missing
entries.snippet: The UN migration agency has reported that at least 109 people were killed and 116 remain missing after a migrant boat sank overnight on its way to Yemen. At least 80 Ethiopians survived the incident but 15 children died.

entries.title: Poland on alert amid possible attack on PM, defense minister
entries.snippet: Poland was holding an emergency meeting after police received information about a possible assassination plot against PM Donald Tusk. The meeting comes amid a wave of violence at Polish schools this week.

entries.title: Pakistan: President puts Khan stronghold province under emergency rule
entries.snippet: President Asif Ali Zardari has effectively suspended the provincial government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The northwestern state is an epicenter of support for former PM Imran Khan and run by his PTI party.

entries.title: Yemen's Houthis warn passengers not to use Saudi airports
entries.snippet: The warning from the Iran-backed rebels comes a day after a missile attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and injured more than 300. The airport will remain closed until at least Sunday night.

entries.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump diesel deal
entries.snippet: After Washington announced a sanctions pause on Russian diesel, Germany has said it remains committed to pressuring Moscow and supporting Ukraine. More on DW.

entries.title: Couples looking to have children often turn to surrogacy agencies in Georgia without understanding the hidden costs
entries.snippet: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

entries.title: Demographic change: Germany's population is declining, but not everywhere
entries.snippet: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers, and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.

entries.title: Ukrainian prisoners of war and defectors have been gathered into a Russian battalion to face Ukrainian forces — why? And how?
entries.snippet: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

entries.title: India's 'Cockroach' movement leaders say 'the fight has just begun' after a large protest in Delhi
entries.snippet: Leaders of the youth-led protest movement demanding India's election commissioner step down say the "fight has just begun" after they were released from detention following a large demonstration in Delhi. More on DW.

entries.title: US: Justice Department probes Trump's press pool boycott for antitrust violation
entries.snippet: The Department of Justice is investigating whether the five news organizations violated antitrust laws when they suspended their coverage of Trump in protest. The networks under probe are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News.

entries.title: Shooter kills 8 people and himself in Pennsylvania — police
entries.snippet: The 45-year-old shooter, who is yet to be identified, carried out the killings at his home in Erie. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro offered support as the lakeside city grieves.

entries.title: Storm Isaias leaves 4 dead as it moves across southern US
entries.snippet: The storm, which is now a post-tropical cyclone, had made landfall near Destin, Florida on Friday evening. The storm brings heavy rainfall and powerful winds and has caused mass power outages in Florida and Alabama.

entries.title: Palestinian president postpones elections until late 2027
entries.snippet: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas previously committed to holding legislative elections in November 2026. He said that due to "obstacles ⁠posed by Israeli measures" the vote would be pushed back until late next year.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia: 12 killed, hundreds injured in Riyadh airport attack
entries.snippet: A Saudi-led coalition has vowed a "decisive" response after the deadliest strike on Saudi soil in over a decade. Officials have pinned the attack on Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen.

entries.title: Money, networks and bias: Why women struggle to win seats in US politics
entries.snippet: The US is holding Congress and state governors elections. At all levels of US politics, women are underrepresented — but they may win some historic victories in the midterms on November 3.

entries.title: Eritrea urges UN deterrence measures against Ethiopia
entries.snippet: Eritrea has officially requested UN Security Council assistance over the conflict in Tigray. Both Eritrea and Ethiopia accuse each other of fueling regional instability.

entries.title: Trump slams Zelenskyy, says Ukraine should elect new president
entries.snippet: President Trump has criticized Volodymyr Zelenskyy for not making a deal with Russia to end the Ukraine war. Trump also warned Kyiv against targeting Russian oil refineries that will supply the US with diesel fuel.

entries.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
entries.snippet: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

entries.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
entries.snippet: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.
